# spring-blueprint

> A working Spring Boot 4 microservice in Java 25 that doubles as a reference Gradle build and an experimentation sandbox. It exists to be cloned as the starting point for new projects, to demonstrate Spring Boot layering and design patterns, and to serve as a stable base for trying out new technologies, CI/CD workflows, and cloud deployments.

Key facts for working in this repository:

- Single Gradle subproject named `app`, which holds the ENTIRE application build, so `./gradlew build` and `./gradlew :app:build` are equivalent. The root `build.gradle.kts` exists but is deliberately minimal: it applies spotless to the root Gradle scripts and does nothing else. Do NOT move application configuration into it.
- There are TWO spotless configurations, and that is not duplication. A spotless target resolves relative to the project that declares it, and spotless hard-rejects anything outside it ("All target files must be within the project dir"), so `app`'s block can never lint `settings.gradle.kts` however its target is written. The root block covers `settings.gradle.kts` + the root `build.gradle.kts`; the `app` block covers `app/build.gradle.kts` plus all of `src/**`. `:app:check` dependsOn `rootProject.tasks.spotlessCheck`, which is what makes the root scripts binding for bootJar, build, release, and CI (CI runs `:app:check`, not the unqualified `check`).
- Always use the wrapper `./gradlew` (Gradle 9.7.1). Compilation and tests run on an auto-provisioned Java 25 Microsoft Build of OpenJDK toolchain, independent of the JDK running Gradle.
- The `libs` version catalog is NOT a local `gradle/libs.versions.toml`. It resolves from the published catalog `com.rubensgomes:gradle-catalog`, declared in `settings.gradle.kts`. Never hard-code a plugin or library version in the build script.
- Library versions are supplied by the Spring Boot BOM imported via `platform(libs.spring.boot.bom)`. Dependency coordinates deliberately omit versions.
- A `platform()` import applies only to the configuration it is declared on and configurations extending it. `annotationProcessor`, `testAnnotationProcessor`, and `developmentOnly` extend nothing and import the BOM explicitly. A versionless dependency added to any other standalone configuration must do the same, or it fails with `Could not find <group>:<name>:` and no version.
- Dependency locking is active and enforced in `LockMode.STRICT`. FOUR lock files pin every resolved version: `settings-gradle.lockfile` (version catalog), `buildscript-gradle.lockfile` at the ROOT (the root build script's plugin classpath -- spotless), `app/gradle.lockfile` (application graph — `annotationProcessor`, `compileClasspath`, `developmentOnly`, `runtimeClasspath`, `testAnnotationProcessor`, `testCompileClasspath`, `testRuntimeClasspath`), and `app/buildscript-gradle.lockfile` (the `:app` plugin classpath). All four are committed.
- Regenerate lock state with `./gradlew :app:dependencies --write-locks` after adding or removing a dependency, after changing the `com.rubensgomes:gradle-catalog` version in `settings.gradle.kts` (the Spring Boot BOM version flows from the catalog, so the whole transitive closure shifts), or after changing which configurations are locked. It requires `GITHUB_USER` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` and cannot run with `--offline`. Never pass `--write-locks` in an automated build.
- NEVER hand-edit a lock file. A lock file is a forcing constraint, not a checksum: where the lock and the Spring Boot BOM disagree the lock wins, so changing a version to another version that exists silently changes the build instead of failing it. A missing entry fails with `Resolved '<coords>' which is not part of the dependency lock state`; a missing file fails with `Locking strict mode: Configuration '<name>' is locked but does not have lock state.` Both mean: regenerate.
- Spotless entries live in the ROOT `buildscript-gradle.lockfile`, NOT in `app/buildscript-gradle.lockfile`, even though `app` applies and uses spotless heavily. This is correct, not a mistake: a subproject inherits the root project's buildscript classpath, so once the root script applies spotless, `:app` no longer resolves it itself and its lock file legitimately stops listing it. Bumping the spotless version in the catalog therefore requires regenerating the ROOT lock file (`./gradlew :dependencies --write-locks`), not the `:app` one.
- `LockMode.STRICT` is set TWICE in `app/build.gradle.kts` — once inside `buildscript { }` and once on the project extension. This is not duplication. The project-level mode does not reach the buildscript classpath; with only that one set, deleting `app/buildscript-gradle.lockfile` leaves the build passing silently. Both lines are load-bearing.
- The equivalent buildscript-locking block does NOT work in `settings.gradle.kts`: plugins requested through the settings `plugins { }` block do not pass through the settings buildscript classpath, so it locks an empty configuration and writes no lock state. It was tried and removed; do not re-add it.
- Docker: multi-stage `Dockerfile` (builder on `mcr.microsoft.com/openjdk/jdk:25-ubuntu`, extractor + runtime on `eclipse-temurin:25-jre-alpine`) plus `docker-compose.yml`. Run with `docker compose up --build -d`. The builder base and the toolchain vendor are ONE decision: the build pins `vendor = JvmVendorSpec.MICROSOFT`, this base reports `java.vendor` `Microsoft`, and any other vendor makes the foojay resolver download a second ~200 MB JDK on every cold build. The Dockerfile passes `-Porg.gradle.java.installations.auto-download=false` so that mistake fails fast instead. Changing `vendor` in `app/build.gradle.kts` without changing `FROM` breaks `docker build` while host builds stay green.
- The Docker builder stage installs no extra packages: the Ubuntu-based Microsoft JDK image already ships `find` and `xargs`. Both are hard requirements -- the Gradle wrapper aborts with `xargs is not available` before doing anything else, and the jar-selection step uses `find`. A slimmer base (`25-distroless`, or an Amazon Linux *minimal* image, which is why a `dnf install -y findutils` line used to be here) reintroduces that problem.
- `./gradlew dockerBuild` is a plain `Exec` task shelling out to the `docker` CLI. It does NOT depend on `bootJar` (the Dockerfile compiles in its own builder stage, so depending on the host jar would run the suite twice) and is NOT a dependency of `build` (so an ordinary build never needs a Docker daemon). Do not replace it with `com.bmuschko.docker-remote-api` -- that plugin uses the Engine API's legacy builder, which has no `--mount=type=secret`, so the in-container Gradle build would fail on the version catalog with a 401.
- The Docker build REQUIRES `GITHUB_USER` and `GITHUB_TOKEN`, passed as BuildKit secrets (`--secret id=github_user,env=GITHUB_USER`). A Docker build always starts with a cold Gradle cache, and every plugin resolves through the remote version catalog, so nothing resolves without them. They are build-time only and never enter an image layer.
- `bootJar` depends on `check`, so `docker build` runs spotless, the full JUnit suite and the 90% coverage gate inside the builder stage. This is deliberate. `--build-arg GRADLE_BUILD_ARGS="-x check"` is a local-iteration escape hatch that CI must never set. It is also why `app/src/test` and `.editorconfig` must stay in the Docker build context.
- Spring Boot 4 REMOVED the `layertools` jarmode. Layer extraction is `java -Djarmode=tools -jar application.jar extract --layers --launcher --destination <dir>`. `--destination` must not already exist or be non-empty.
- `application-docker.yml` (profile `docker`, activated by `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE`) exists mainly because the default profile pins `logging.level.root` to `error`. Without it a container prints the banner and nothing else, which looks like a hang. Anything deployment-specific belongs in `docker-compose.yml`, not in that file.
- The container `ENTRYPOINT` is exec form so the JVM is PID 1 and SIGTERM reaches Spring's graceful shutdown. Never wrap it in `sh -c` to expand a variable: `sh` does not forward SIGTERM. Use `JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS` for JVM flags instead.
- Three Spring profiles. `application.yml` (default) pins `logging.level.root` to `error`, so a bare run prints the banner and NOTHING else -- no "Started App" line -- which looks exactly like a hang. `application-local.yml` (profile `local`, activated automatically by `tasks.bootRun`) and `application-docker.yml` (profile `docker`, baked into the image as `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE`) both exist mainly to raise `root` back to `info`. Any new profile needs the same.
- `logging.level.com.rubensgomes.blueprint` must match the real package. A stale value there applies to nothing and the app's own log statements silently fall back to `root`. NOTE: `app/src/test/resources/application.yml` still carries the old `com.rubensgomes.sample` spelling.
- `spring.application.name` in `application.yml` is the build-time token `@artifactId@`, replaced at `processResources` by `ReplaceTokens` from the `artifactId` property in `app/gradle.properties`. Editing the literal has no effect. `@...@` delimiters are used rather than Gradle's `expand()` because `expand()` evaluates `${...}`, which collides with Spring's own placeholder syntax. The filter matches `application*.yml`, so every profile file passes through it.
- Every failed request returns JSON, never Spring Boot's Whitelabel HTML. The `/error` mapping enumerates its HTTP methods (`GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `OPTIONS`) instead of using the `@RequestMapping` default. DO NOT narrow that list to `GET`: the container forwards the ORIGINAL request method when dispatching to `/error`, so a failed POST arrives as a POST, and a GET-only mapping would turn every non-GET failure into a 405 instead of the real status. `TRACE` is omitted deliberately (cross-site tracing). The unit tests call `handleError` directly and do NOT exercise the mapping, so they will not catch a regression here -- verify against a running server. `GlobalErrorController` implements `org.springframework.boot.webmvc.error.ErrorController` (NOTE: Spring Boot 4 moved this out of `org.springframework.boot.web.servlet.error`) and maps `/error`; the body type is the `ErrorResponse` record. This changes only the error representation -- an unmapped path still returns 404.
- Project properties live in two files: `app/gradle.properties` (coordinates, version) and the root `gradle.properties` (developer identity, license, SCM, SonarQube, Gradle daemon). Read them with the `gradleProperty(name)` helper in `app/build.gradle.kts`. Note that `providers.gradleProperty(...)` does NOT resolve values from a subproject `gradle.properties`; the helper uses `findProperty` for that reason.
- `check` is a real gate: Spotless format verification, the JUnit 5 suite, and a JaCoCo rule requiring 90% line and 90% branch coverage. `bootJar`, `assemble`, `build`, and `release` all depend on it, so packaging runs the full verification.
- Spotless verifies but never rewrites during compilation. Run `./gradlew spotlessApply` to format. Badly formatted code fails the build.
- The header comment in `app/build.gradle.kts` is a plain block comment, not KDoc. ktlint's `standard:kdoc` rule rejects KDoc at the top level of a Gradle script.
- `GITHUB_USER` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are required to resolve dependencies on a cold cache and to publish. `SONAR_TOKEN` is required only by the `sonar` task. `sonar.qualitygate.wait=true` makes that task block until SonarCloud finishes processing and fail the build on a failing gate, so it runs as long as server-side analysis rather than returning at upload.
- The Gradle configuration cache is disabled because the release plugin is incompatible with it.
- The project is licensed **MIT** (it was Apache-2.0 until 2026-08-24). Source files carry an `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` header plus an AI-generated-content notice pointing at `LICENSE`. The header text is the `licenseHeaderText` constant in `app/build.gradle.kts`; Spotless injects and verifies it on the `java` and `kotlin` formats, which target `src/**` ONLY -- the headers in `settings.gradle.kts` and `app/build.gradle.kts` are NOT Spotless-managed and must be hand-edited.
- Changing the project license means changing EIGHT places, not one: the root `LICENSE` file; `licenseHeaderText` in `app/build.gradle.kts` (then `./gradlew spotlessApply` to restamp `src/**`); `license`/`licenseUrl` in the root `gradle.properties` (these feed the POM `<licenses>` of every published artifact); the `org.opencontainers.image.licenses` label in the `Dockerfile`; the header comments in BOTH `.github/workflows/build-verify.yml` and `.github/workflows/release.yml`; and the hand-maintained headers at the top of `settings.gradle.kts` and `app/build.gradle.kts`.
- The license header at the top of `app/build.gradle.kts`, `settings.gradle.kts` and the root `build.gradle.kts` is MERGED into the same block comment as each script's documentation header, separated by a dashed rule. Do NOT split it into two adjacent block comments, and do NOT make either half KDoc. Two ktlint rules apply to every Gradle script and both FAIL the build rather than auto-fixing: `standard:no-consecutive-comments` ("a block comment may not be preceded by a block comment") and `standard:kdoc` ("A KDoc is not allowed inside 'block'"). `settings.gradle.kts` had a KDoc header that went undetected until the root spotless block started linting it.
- `LICENSE` carries more than the MIT grant: AI-generated content, third-party content, copyright-status, limitation-of-liability, and no-warranty notices. `DISCLAIMER.md` carries an overlapping general disclaimer.
- There are TWO workflows with opposite postures. `build-verify.yml` triggers on every push to `main` and is read-only (`permissions: contents: read`). `release.yml` is `workflow_dispatch` ONLY and WRITES to the repository (`contents: write`) -- it pushes two commits, a tag, and the `release` branch. They share the same three setup steps (checkout / setup-java `distribution: microsoft` 25 / setup-gradle), the same `GRADLE_ARGS`, and the same `PACKAGES_USER`/`PACKAGES_TOKEN` credential carriers; changing one usually means changing the other.
- CI is `.github/workflows/build-verify.yml`: one job (`build-verify`) on `ubuntu-latest`, triggered on push to `main` only. After checkout / setup-java / setup-gradle it runs FOUR separate `./gradlew` invocations in order -- `:app:classes :app:testClasses`, `:app:test`, `:app:check`, `:app:sonar`. This is deliberate, not redundant: `sonar` dependsOn `check` dependsOn `test`, so each step finds the previous step's work UP-TO-DATE (up-to-date state persists in `app/.gradle`, not in daemon memory) and adds only its own; the payoff is four independently red/green steps. Verified locally: `test` does NOT re-run during the `check` step, and Spotless runs once.
- The CI workflow CANNOT declare `GITHUB_USER` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` in an `env:` block -- GitHub Actions reserves the `GITHUB_` prefix. The values ride in `PACKAGES_USER` / `PACKAGES_TOKEN` (from the org secret `RUBENS_PAT_TOKEN`) and each step `export`s the real names into its own shell. Both are needed by EVERY invocation because `settings.gradle.kts` reads them at settings-evaluation time.
- The CI steps pin `shell: bash` because they expand `$GRADLE_ARGS` unquoted and depend on word splitting. bash splits an unquoted expansion; zsh does NOT, and under zsh the whole string arrives as one argument (`Argument value '...' given for --console option is invalid`).
- CI installs the JDK with `actions/setup-java` `distribution: microsoft`, `java-version: 25`, to satisfy the `JvmVendorSpec.MICROSOFT` pin, and passes `-Porg.gradle.java.installations.auto-download=false` exactly as the Dockerfile does. The toolchain vendor now has THREE call sites that must move together: `app/build.gradle.kts`, the Dockerfile `FROM`, and the workflow's `distribution:`.
- CI passes `--console=plain -Dorg.gradle.logging.level=lifecycle` to override `org.gradle.console=verbose` and `org.gradle.logging.level=info` from gradle.properties without editing that file. Verified: command-line sources outrank the project gradle.properties.
- `actions/checkout` uses `fetch-depth: 0` in CI. SonarCloud derives New Code detection, blame and issue backdating from git history, and silently degrades on a shallow clone rather than failing.
- The release plugin pushes two commits per release to `main`, so each release triggers ~2 extra CI runs. Accepted so the trigger stays a literal "on push"; `build-verify.yml`'s closing comment carries the `if:` guard that suppresses them.
- `release.yml` is one job (`release`) whose substantive step is `./gradlew release`. Four things it needs that `build-verify.yml` does not, all load-bearing: (1) `permissions: contents: write`, because it pushes; (2) checkout with `ref: main` AND `fetch-depth: 0` -- `requireBranch` is `main` and the plugin diffs local against remote, so a shallow or detached checkout breaks the branch check and tag creation; (3) checkout with `token: ${{ secrets.RUBENS_PAT_TOKEN }}`, because the token checkout persists is what the plugin's own `git push` uses; (4) a `git config user.name`/`user.email` step, because the plugin makes two commits and a runner has no identity -- without it the release dies at `preTagCommit`. Those two values are read out of `gradle.properties` (`developerName`, `developerEmail`) rather than hardcoded.
- `release.yml` deliberately uses a PAT rather than the automatic per-run `GITHUB_TOKEN`. A push made with the automatic token does NOT trigger other workflows (GitHub suppresses that to prevent recursion), so the released commit would never be verified by `build-verify.yml`. The cost is the ~2 extra `build-verify` runs per release noted above.
- A release needs `release.useAutomaticVersion=true` (root `gradle.properties`). Without it the plugin prompts interactively for the version and the CI job HANGS until it times out.
- Two things stop a first release: `workflow_dispatch` does not appear at all until the workflow file is on the DEFAULT branch, and branch protection on `main` will reject the plugin's push unless the PAT is exempt.

## Documentation

- [README.md](README.md): Project purpose, technology stack, demonstrated design patterns, testing approach, template instructions, and roadmap.
- [BUILD.md](BUILD.md): Complete Gradle build reference — every task, when it runs, how to invoke it, where configuration lives, the build lifecycle graph, dependency locking and lock-file regeneration, and troubleshooting for common failures.

## Build configuration

- [settings.gradle.kts](settings.gradle.kts): Project inclusion, plugin management, dependency repositories including GitHub Packages, and the shared version catalog declaration.
- [app/build.gradle.kts](app/build.gradle.kts): The entire build — plugins, dependencies, toolchain, jar manifests, JaCoCo coverage rules, Spotless formatting, maven-publish, release, and SonarQube configuration.
- [gradle.properties](gradle.properties): Developer identity, license metadata, GitHub Packages URL, SonarQube coordinates, and Gradle daemon settings shared across the build.
- [app/gradle.properties](app/gradle.properties): Module coordinates — `group`, `version`, `artifactId`, `title`, `description`, `mainClass`, and SCM URLs. The version must end in `-SNAPSHOT` for the release plugin.
- [app/gradle.lockfile](app/gradle.lockfile): Generated lock state for the application dependency graph. Regenerate, never edit.
- [app/buildscript-gradle.lockfile](app/buildscript-gradle.lockfile): Generated lock state for the Gradle plugin classpath. Regenerate, never edit.
- [settings-gradle.lockfile](settings-gradle.lockfile): Generated lock state for the `libs` version catalog resolution. Gradle locks version-catalog configurations automatically; no configuration declares this.
- [Dockerfile](Dockerfile): Multi-stage image build -- Gradle builder, layered-jar extractor, non-root JRE runtime with a HEALTHCHECK against /actuator/health.
- [docker-compose.yml](docker-compose.yml): Local container run -- build secrets, port 8080, the `docker` profile, healthcheck, graceful-shutdown grace period, and resource limits.
- [app/src/main/resources/application-docker.yml](app/src/main/resources/application-docker.yml): Container profile. Restores INFO logging, disables ANSI, enables the liveness/readiness probes.
- [build.gradle.kts](build.gradle.kts): Minimal root script. Applies Spotless to the ROOT Gradle scripts only -- the one thing `app/build.gradle.kts` cannot do, because Spotless rejects targets outside its own project dir. Add nothing else here.
- [buildscript-gradle.lockfile](buildscript-gradle.lockfile): Generated lock state for the ROOT plugin classpath (Spotless). Regenerate with `./gradlew :dependencies --write-locks`, never edit.
- [.github/workflows/build-verify.yml](.github/workflows/build-verify.yml): CI. Push to `main`; read-only; one job `build-verify` running compile, test, check, sonar as four separate `./gradlew` invocations.
- [.github/workflows/release.yml](.github/workflows/release.yml): Release. `workflow_dispatch` ONLY; WRITES to the repo (`contents: write`); one job `release` whose substantive step is `./gradlew release`. Needs `ref: main` + `fetch-depth: 0`, a PAT on checkout, and a configured git identity.
- [.editorconfig](.editorconfig): ktlint formatting rules applied to `*.gradle.kts` by Spotless.

## Application source

- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/App.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/App.java): The `@SpringBootApplication` entry point, referenced by the `mainClass` property.
- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/web/controller/GlobalErrorController.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/web/controller/GlobalErrorController.java): Maps `/error` and renders every container-forwarded failure as JSON. Falls back to 500 and placeholder values when the request attributes are absent or malformed.
- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/model/response/ErrorResponse.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/model/response/ErrorResponse.java): Error body record -- timestamp, status, error, message, path. Field names mirror Spring Boot's default error attributes.
- [app/src/main/resources/application-local.yml](app/src/main/resources/application-local.yml): `local` profile, activated by `bootRun`. Raises `logging.level.root` to `info`.
- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/web/controller/HelloWorldRestController.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/web/controller/HelloWorldRestController.java): REST layer serving `GET /api/v1/helloworld`. Uses constructor injection and delegates all business responsibility to the service layer.
- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/service/HelloWorldService.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/service/HelloWorldService.java): Business layer returning a model response type, with a `@PreDestroy` shutdown hook.
- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/model/response/MessageResponse.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/model/response/MessageResponse.java): A `record` carrying a single `message` component, with Jakarta Bean Validation constraints on the component. Jackson serializes it via the generated accessor, so the wire format is `{"message":"..."}`. The accessor is `message()`, not `getMessage()`.
- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/event/AppInitEventListener.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/event/AppInitEventListener.java): Observer pattern via `ApplicationListener`, logging host and port once the servlet container is initialized.
- [app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/event/AppShutdownEventListener.java](app/src/main/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/event/AppShutdownEventListener.java): Observer pattern handling `ContextClosedEvent` on SIGTERM.
- [app/src/main/resources/application.yml](app/src/main/resources/application.yml): Runtime configuration — port 8080, graceful shutdown, logging levels and groups.

## Optional

- [app/src/test/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/AppTest.java](app/src/test/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/AppTest.java): Full `@SpringBootTest` context load test.
- [app/src/test/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/web/controller/HelloWorldRestControllerTest.java](app/src/test/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/web/controller/HelloWorldRestControllerTest.java): Standalone MockMvc web layer test without booting the application.
- [app/src/test/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/model/response/MessageResponseTest.java](app/src/test/java/com/rubensgomes/blueprint/model/response/MessageResponseTest.java): Nested tests exercising a real Jakarta `Validator`.
- [Spring Boot Gradle plugin](https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/gradle-plugin/index.html): Reference for `bootJar`, `bootRun`, and application packaging.
- [Gradle user guide](https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/userguide.html): Reference for the core plugins used here.
